claude.sample_unit: training cases (iterated 10 to 1000) drawn from UK Biobank
models_evaluated: stacked transfer learning (LASSO penalized logistic regression stacking previously trained CVD, stroke, CKD and diabetes risk models)
de novo LASSO logistic regression on 33 variables

links.outcome: AUC of locally tuned stacked models versus de novo models across small local training sample sizes
links.effect: Stacked models needed roughly one-tenth of the training sample of de novo models. For CVD, stacked reached AUC 0.732 (0.728, 0.735) with 30 cases, versus 300 cases for de novo. The difference was smaller for CKD.
links.quote: We found that stacked models require roughly one-tenths of the training sample size compared to de novo derivation of a prediction model.

models_evaluated: previously trained risk prediction models for cardiovascular disease, stroke, kidney disease, and diabetes

links.effect: Stacked models required roughly one-tenth the training sample size; CVD AUC 0.732 (0.728, 0.735) with 30 cases vs 300 de novo cases.
links.quote: We found that stacked models require roughly one-tenths of the training sample size compared to de novo derivation of a prediction model.

links.outcome: Stacked versus de novo model performance
links.effect: For CVD, stacked model needed 30 cases to reach AUC 0.732 (0.728, 0.735); de novo model needed 300 cases for approximately same performance.
links.quote: For example, predicting CVD the stacked model required 30 cases to reach a area under the curve (AUC) value (with 95% CI) of 0.732 (0.728, 0.735), while the de novo model required 300 cases to reach approximately the same performance.

unlisted_practices: Stacked transfer learning using multiple previously trained risk prediction models to approximate de novo local model derivation with smaller local training samples
